category_title: Independent learners who struggle to visualize spatial relationships in three-dimensional word problems
scenario_title: 3D Truck Problem with 2D Rectangular Prism Diagram
minimal_context: The student is working on a multistep word problem about fitting a long pole in the back of a loading truck using a provided 2D diagram of a rectangular prism.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's look at this next multistep word problem about fitting a long pole in the back of a loading truck. Here is the diagram of the rectangular prism with the labeled dimensions.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Is it still Pythagorean Theorem? I’m not sure yet, because we don’t know the whole truck.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: How would you start setting it up on your scratch paper?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Y eah, by drawing a picture of it like out of the truck. (She drew a triangle using dimensions given, but not the right dimensions.) It’s 5 and 4 as the legs?

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Take another look at the dimensions you chose for that triangle.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Oh man. Y eah, is that supposed to be the way it is farthest in the truck? (Starts to guess again using a different combination of dimensions.) Is the next one going to be in here?
